expectations.text: Every reported problem cites a specific file and line
expectations.evidence: Findings 1-7 and 9-11 all carry bolded `reviewer-core/src/review/summarize.ts:<lines>` headers, and finding 4 gives a per-line TypeScript error table (lines 49, 50, 57, 58, 63, 64). finding_counts_note: total_findings counts the 12 numbered findings; the closing 'Design note' is a restructuring recommendation, not a defect, and is excluded. structural_findings = #1 (provider constructed inside the core / dependency direction), #2 (fs I/O across the package boundary), #7 (model hardcoded in the engine rather than caller-supplied), #8 (missing from the package entry point / public surface). Grounding (#3), compile errors (#4), z.custom (#5), trust wrapping (#6), telemetry (#9), scope filter (#10), plumbing hooks (#11) and tests (#12) counted non-structural. #4-#7 map to answer_key.legitimate_extra_findings; #10 (missing applyScopeFilter) is an additional pipeline-invariant finding not in the answer key but grounded in run.ts:224 and not a decoy, so it is not counted as a false positive.

suggestions.assertion: Does NOT flag the existing llm/openrouter.ts openai SDK import as a violation
suggestions.reason: Passes by silence here, as in without_skill/run-1: openrouter.ts is cited four times as supporting evidence but its own layering status is never assessed. Indistinguishable under the current wording from the two runs that explicitly cleared it. Add a stricter companion assertion.

suggestions.assertion: Every reported problem cites a specific file and line
suggestions.reason: Non-discriminating; identical pass with identical absence-finding exceptions in all four runs.

This run is the only one that actually compiled the fixture (tsc --noEmit against an isolated copy) and reported per-line TS error codes. That is a materially stronger form of evidence than the other three runs' assertion-from-reading, and no assertion rewards it. An assertion like 'the compile-breaking API misuse is demonstrated, not just asserted' would be discriminating.

It is also the most expensive run (87,919 tokens, 298.7s, 37 tool uses vs 71,061/183s/23 for the cheapest) for the same 5/5. Cost per unit of correctness is invisible to the assertion set; if the skill is meant to make reviews cheaper as well as correct, that needs to be measured rather than inferred.

eval_feedback.overall: 5/5. Every run in this iteration passes every assertion, so the assertions themselves carry no signal here. The real differences — decoy cleared vs unmentioned, finding volume, whether the compile claim was demonstrated, and token cost — are all outside the current assertion set.
